findings.reason: the plan should name these owners and say whether the new call reuses or extends them instead of leaving a second cost/retry path beside the first.
findings.text: §25 places the decisions call layer in the module that already owns cost and retry policy but re-derives both: "returns the answers and the cost from `usage.cost`" duplicates `extract_cost` (llm.py:1616), and "429 and 5xx responses retry with backoff" duplicates `_is_retryable` (llm.py:1188) and `_is_rate_limited` (llm.py:1215); the guard pattern it cites is reckon's `tests/test_suite_never_calls_live_jev.py` while this repo already has `set_litellm_offline_env` (llm.py:831) and the §23 prompt-schema coverage test (tests/llm/test_prompt_schema_coverage.py) as in-tree precedents

findings.reason: the author must name the owner being extended or retired, else two threshold owners coexist for one gate and the default-0.75 path silently outlives its purpose.
findings.text: the code triage/ingest gates already have owners (`min_triage_score: float = 0.75` at state.py:29; `get_triage_threshold()` at imas_codex/settings.py:1009, derived from `[tool.imas-codex.discovery].triage-offset`; `get_discovery_threshold()` at settings.py:997), and §25 adds `code-triage-threshold` (0.4) and `code-ingest-threshold` (0.6) in the same `[tool.imas-codex.discovery]` block without naming whether `min_triage_score`, `get_triage_threshold` or `triage-offset` are retired or extended — the existing triage threshold is read at workers.py:314/349/975, parallel.py:137/174/428, graph_ops.py:403/695 and scorer.py:468-470

findings.reason: without naming the retirement the plan leaves a dead prompt/batch/helpers behind and reddens the prompt-coverage guard the plan itself landed one section earlier.
findings.text: §25 "replaces the code triage stage's LLM call with the names-arm decision" but names no owner it orphans: the existing triage decision is owned by `get_model("discovery-triage")` + `call_llm_structured` (workers.py:235), the prompt `imas_codex/llm/prompts/code/triage.md`, and `FileTriageBatch`/`_build_triage_system_prompt`/`apply_triage_results` in imas_codex/discovery/code/scorer.py; orphaning `triage.md` also removes a registered prompt that §23's landed guard (tests/llm/test_prompt_schema_coverage.py, landed 5cfab2ce7) asserts is rendered somewhere

findings.reason: the section must state what the new seat supersedes or why nothing can, so the seat registry does not grow a second triage-adjacent name with no retirement line.
findings.text: §25 adds the seat `discovery-relevance` to the `MODEL_SECTIONS` registry (settings.py:144) with defaults (settings.py:172) and an env var (settings.py:214), a public-interface addition, and neither names a seat it retires or merges nor states why none can be; the existing `discovery-triage` seat (settings.py:144, used at workers.py:235) loses its code-file call to the new seat and is left unaccounted

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `call_decisions`/`acall_decisions` hide POST, backoff, answer validation and cost extraction behind two functions and return `(answers, cost)`; that is a small interface over substantial behaviour, not a spread of shallow wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §25 adds `code-triage-threshold`/`code-ingest-threshold` and replaces the code-triage LLM call without naming the existing owners of those two decisions (`min_triage_score`/`get_triage_threshold`/`triage-offset`, and `workers.py:235` + `code/triage.md` + `FileTriageBatch`).
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0 (read 2026-10-06T15:50:45Z); §25 adds a seat to the `MODEL_SECTIONS` registry without naming any seat it retires or merges, or stating why none can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §25 proposes `call_decisions`/`acall_decisions` in `imas_codex/discovery/base/llm.py` and new cost/retry handling beside owners already in that file (`extract_cost`, `_is_retryable`, `_is_rate_limited`, `set_litellm_offline_env`), and cites another repository's live-call guard instead of this repo's own offline mechanism.
